name: Cup and handle
shape: A rounded bottom, then a small pause just below the lid.
description: This screen looks for a stock that fell away, curved back up over several weeks, and then paused briefly near the top of that curve. The curve is the cup and the pause is the handle. Three things are checked rather than assumed: the low sits in the middle of the base and not at either edge, because a low at the left edge is a recovery and a low at the right edge is still a fall; both sides come back to a similar height; and the pause near the end is shallow and sits high in the cup, because a deep late drop is a second leg down. It is the most recognisable shape here and, like the others, it is a description rather than a forecast.

concepts.title: The cup
concepts.text: A fall and a gradual curve back up over several weeks.

concepts.title: Rounded, not V-shaped
concepts.text: The low sits in the middle of the span, so it curved rather than snapped back.

concepts.title: The rims
concepts.text: The two sides of the cup, both near the same height.

concepts.title: The handle
concepts.text: A short, shallow pause near the top of the cup before it tries to clear it.

funnel.title: The liquid US universe
funnel.text: US common stocks over $5, market cap over $300M, and at least $5M traded a day over the last 20 sessions.

funnel.title: Leadership
funnel.text: Relative strength rating of 70 or better.

funnel.title: Where we look for the ceiling
funnel.text: The pivot is the highest price of the last 40 weeks.

funnel.title: Long enough to round out
funnel.text: The cup has taken at least 7 weeks.

funnel.title: Not a collapse
funnel.text: From its ceiling, the base never fell more than 35%.

funnel.title: Rounded, not a V
funnel.text: At least 0.18 of the sessions closed in the lower part of the cup.

funnel.title: Both rims near the lid
funnel.text: Neither side of the cup sits more than 8% below the top.

funnel.title: A brief handle
funnel.text: The pause at the end lasted no more than 4 weeks.

funnel.title: A shallow handle
funnel.text: The pause gave back no more than 15% of its own range.

funnel.title: High in the cup
funnel.text: The handle's low sits at least 0.5 of the way up from the bottom of the cup.

funnel.title: Above its 50-day line
funnel.text: Price is above the average of the last 50 days.

funnel.title: Near the trigger
funnel.text: Price is no more than 20% below the pivot.

funnel_preface: Every number below is a dial you can move in Filters.

params.label: Lowest RS rating we'll accept
params.funnel_text: Relative strength rating of {value} or better.
params.help: Where the stock's 3, 6 and 12-month return ranks against every other name in the universe, 1 to 99. This is the one filter with published statistical support behind it.

params.label: How far back to look for the ceiling
params.funnel_title: Where we look for the ceiling
params.funnel_text: The pivot is the highest price of the last {value} weeks.
params.help: The window we search for the price the stock has to clear. A longer window finds older, larger structures.

params.label: Shortest cup we'll accept
params.funnel_text: The cup has taken at least {value} weeks.
params.help: A curve needs time. Anything faster is a dip, and it cannot round.

params.label: Deepest base we'll accept
params.funnel_text: From its ceiling, the base never fell more than {value}%.
params.help: How far price dropped inside the base, measured from the ceiling to the lowest point. Deeper structures take longer to repair.

params.label: How much of the cup is spent near the bottom
params.funnel_text: At least {value} of the sessions closed in the lower part of the cup.
params.help: A V has its low in the middle too. What separates them is time: a cup lingers near the bottom, a V passes through it in a few days.

params.label: Furthest a rim may sit below the lid
params.funnel_text: Neither side of the cup sits more than {value}% below the top.
params.help: If the left side is far lower, the stock is still climbing back to where it was rather than rounding out.

params.label: Longest handle we'll accept
params.funnel_text: The pause at the end lasted no more than {value} weeks.
params.help: A pause that runs for months is not a handle, it is another base.

params.label: Deepest handle we'll accept
params.funnel_text: The pause gave back no more than {value}% of its own range.
params.help: A deep drop at the end is a second leg down, not a rest.

params.label: How high in the cup the handle must sit
params.funnel_text: The handle's low sits at least {value} of the way up from the bottom of the cup.
params.help: 0.5 means the handle never dipped below the middle of the cup. Back at the bottom, it is not a handle.

params.label: Must be above its 50-day line
params.funnel_text: Price is above the average of the last 50 days.
params.help: The average closing price of the last 50 sessions.

params.label: How far below the pivot we still list it
params.funnel_text: Price is no more than {value}% below the pivot.
params.help: How close the stock currently sits to the price it has to clear.

params.label: Smallest swing that counts as a contraction
params.help: A move smaller than this is treated as noise rather than as a pullback, so the contraction list stays readable.

params.label: How recent counts as fresh
params.help: A breakout stays in the fresh bucket for this many sessions before it moves to climbing.

params.label: Moving averages that must be in order
params.funnel_text: At least {value} of the three rungs hold — 9 above 21, 21 above 50, 50 above 200.
params.help: The 9, 21, 50 and 200-day averages, fastest to slowest. Three of three is a full stack: every timeframe pointing the same way. Zero turns this off, which is where it starts, so no screen changes until you move it. A stock with under 200 sessions of history has no 200-day average and is not judged on this at all.

trade_steps.title: Buy the breakout
trade_steps.text: As it pushes through the pivot.

trade_steps.title: Set a safety net
trade_steps.text: An automatic exit if it drops about 8% from where you got in.

trade_steps.title: Lock in "no loss"
trade_steps.text: Once it is up enough, move that net to where you started.

trade_steps.title: Ride the trend
trade_steps.text: Raise the net as it climbs.

trade_steps_preface: Risk is decided before entry — about 1.5% of capital on any one trade.
